import re, pathlib

# The 13 reds, minus the two the runner fix and the exact-stdout shape cover on their own.
TESTS = [
    "test_a_wrapper_without_a_context_property_is_still_deprecated",
    "test_csv_escape_deprecation_comes_after_the_control_validation",
    "test_csv_escape_deprecation_is_gated_by_php_version",
    "test_csv_family_deprecates_an_omitted_escape_argument",
    "test_iconv_filter_refusal_uses_the_create_or_locate_wording",
    "test_path_readers_name_themselves_in_unresolvable_filter_warnings",
    "test_run_time_filter_warning_count_follows_the_open_mode_directions",
    "test_stream_filter_strip_tags_is_not_a_php_filter",
    "test_stream_select_refuses_a_memory_stream",
    "test_unresolvable_host_warns_twice_like_php",
    "test_zip_wrapper_reads_entries_and_refuses_like_php",
]

path = pathlib.Path('tests/codegen/io/streams.rs')
text = path.read_text()
parts = re.split(r'(?=\n#\[test\])', text)
sites = 0
out_parts = []
for part in parts:
    name = re.search(r'\nfn (test_\w+)\(', part)
    if not name or name.group(1) not in TESTS:
        out_parts.append(part)
        continue
    lines = part.split('\n')
    new_lines = []
    for line in lines:
        # `assert!(x.success, "...", x.stderr)` is NOT a diagnostic assertion: when a program
        # fails, the uncaught-exception report is on stderr and that is the useful message.
        if '.success,' in line or '.success)' in line:
            new_lines.append(line)
            continue
        if '.stderr' in line:
            fixed = re.sub(r'\b(\w+)\.stderr\b', r'\1.diagnostics', line)
            if fixed != line:
                sites += fixed.count('.diagnostics') - line.count('.diagnostics')
            new_lines.append(fixed)
            continue
        new_lines.append(line)
    out_parts.append('\n'.join(new_lines))
new_text = ''.join(out_parts)
if new_text != text:
    path.write_text(new_text)
print(f"migrated {sites} sites across {len(TESTS)} named tests")
